newsitem.title: UK: EBRD grants Cadbury $70 mln Russian loan.
newsitem.headline: EBRD grants Cadbury $70 mln Russian loan.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it was extending a $70 million loan to Cadbury ZAO, a Russian unit of Britain's Cadbury Schweppes Plc for the completion of a chocolate plant in Novgorod region.

The EBRD said in a statement the loan, of which $25 million had been syndicated to a group of international banks, would be used to complete the construction, commissioning and operation of the $150 million plant, built to European Union environmental standards.
"Russia is currently the third largest chocolate market in Europe," said Hans Christian Jacobsen, director of EBRD's Agribusiness team.

"By setting up a manufacturing site in Russia, Cadbury will have a strong transition impact on the local economy, not only in terms of skills and technology transfer, but also within the retail industry itself with enhanced product access and consistent pricing," he added.
The statement said the EBRD had acted as arranger for the syndication which included Citibank, Credit Suisse and ING Bank as the participating banks..

"We received strong interest from the banking market for this project, the 14th arranged by the EBRD for a Russian borrower involving commercial banks in the financing," said Noreen Doyle, EBRD's deputy vice president for credit and commercial co-financing.

The statement said Cadbury would also lease up to seven warehouses near distributions centres to allow timely deliveries. Up to 80 percent of the products are expected to be sold through local distributors.
Cadbury ZAO is owned by Cadbury Russia Ltd, a joint venture between Cadbury Schweppes and Silbury, an independent distrubuting company in Russia. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
